analysis.title: Rates Spark: Can AI confidence bring rates back up?
key_insights: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on 17 November 2026, followed a day later by Anthropic's IPO. ING treats both as major AI events that now matter for macro and rates.
Nvidia is 5% of S&P 500 market capitalisation, so its results are an important bellwether for the AI story.
The 10yr UST yield is still down from its October highs after AI-related jitters. With the NASDAQ up again, ING thinks US and EUR rates can head back toward their previous peaks.
If Nvidia earnings don't disappoint and Anthropic's IPO succeeds, ING says bonds are unlikely to come out as a winner.
A failure to meet high AI expectations could trigger a significant move lower in rates. Markets pricing a 50bp hike in December are tied to confidence that AI will keep supporting the US economy.

An AI-driven risk-off event would likely pull down euro rates too. ING suggests fading such moves, especially at the front end, because the ECB's reaction function is driven more by inflation than growth and AI has a small footprint in eurozone growth.
The exception to fading euro rates moves is a risk-sentiment shock that also hurts French government bonds. In that case a more dovish market position could be warranted.
